description: MyAgents - Unified AI agent interaction hub with WebSocket CLI connector, agent-to-agent messaging, permissions, voice input, and quality-of-life features

userStories.title: Add Node and Agent models to Prisma schema
userStories.description: As a developer, I need database models for connected machines (nodes) and registered agents so the system can track agent infrastructure.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Node model: id, name, userId (relation to User), lastSeen DateTime, status enum (online/offline)

Add Agent model: id, slug (unique per user), name, description, type enum (hermes/openclaw/custom), nodeId (relation to Node), userId (relation to User), status enum (online/offline), adapterConfig Json (optional), shared Boolean (default false)
Validate slug format: [a-zA-Z0-9-]+ only (no '/' or spaces) — add @db constraint or application-level validation
Add unique constraint on (userId, slug) — slugs are unique per user, not globally
Add proper indexes on Node.userId, Agent.nodeId, Agent.slug, Agent.userId
Generate and run migration successfully
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Foundation for all agent features. Check solved problems for Prisma schema guidelines.

userStories.title: Add Conversation and Message models to Prisma schema
userStories.description: As a developer, I need database models for conversations and messages so users can chat with agents.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Conversation model: id, title (optional), createdAt, updatedAt, userId (relation to User), agentId (relation to Agent)
Add Message model: id, conversationId (relation to Conversation), senderType enum (user/agent), senderId String, content String (text), createdAt
Add proper indexes on Conversation.userId, Conversation.agentId, Message.conversationId
Generate and run migration successfully
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 for Agent model.

userStories.title: Add AgentPermission and ApiKey models to Prisma schema
userStories.description: As a developer, I need models for agent-to-agent permissions and API key authentication.
acceptanceCriteria: Add AgentPermission model: id, agentId (relation to Agent), targetAgentId (relation to Agent), createdBy (relation to User), createdAt — permissions can cross user boundaries
Add unique constraint on (agentId, targetAgentId)
Add ApiKey model: id, keyHash String, name String, userId (relation to User), createdAt, lastUsedAt (optional)
Ensure User model has a unique username field matching [a-zA-Z0-9-]+ (no '/' or spaces) — add if not present, enforce at signup
Generate and run migration successfully
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-001 for Agent model. Username field is needed for cross-user agent addressing (username/agentslug format).

userStories.title: Permission model server-side enforcement
userStories.description: As a developer, I need server-side permission checks so agents can only communicate with explicitly allowed targets, including across user boundaries.
acceptanceCriteria: Add oRPC routes: permission.grant(agentId, targetAgentId), permission.revoke(agentId, targetAgentId), permission.list(agentId)
Permissions are directional: A→B does not imply B→A
Default deny: no agent can talk to any other agent without explicit permission
Same-user permissions: user can freely grant permissions between their own agents
Cross-user permissions: user can grant their agent permission to message another user's agent ONLY if that agent has shared=true
Add agent.share and agent.unshare routes to toggle an agent's shared flag
All permission routes require authentication
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Uses AgentPermission model from US-003. Cross-user sharing requires both sides to opt in: owner shares the agent, other user grants their agent permission.

Return only permitted agents — agents cannot see agents they are not allowed to talk to
User requests (from web app) see all their own agents + a 'Shared with me' section showing other users' shared agents they have permissions for
Unshared agents belonging to other users are never visible
Returned agents include owner username for cross-user agents (displayed as username/slug)
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Depends on US-026. No information leaks — agents only see permitted targets. Cross-user agents display as username/slug.

userStories.title: In-browser Whisper integration using whisper-web
userStories.description: As a developer, I need client-side speech-to-text using the whisper-web approach (transformers.js + Whisper WASM/WebGPU).
acceptanceCriteria: Integrate @huggingface/transformers for in-browser Whisper inference, following whisper-web's experimental-webgpu branch architecture
Use WebGPU backend for GPU-accelerated inference when available, fall back to WASM
Use a Web Worker for transcription to keep the UI thread responsive (reference whisper-web's worker pattern)
No audio leaves the device — all processing is local
Default to whisper-base.en model; support whisper-large-v3-turbo on WebGPU-capable devices
Create a useWhisper hook that handles model loading, audio processing, and transcription
Handle devices without WebGPU gracefully (fall back to WASM), show 'not supported' if neither available
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Privacy-first: all audio processing is client-side. Reference implementation is at ../whisper-web/ (sibling repo, on experimental-webgpu branch with GPU acceleration). Use kctx to query whisper-web for architecture patterns (worker setup, model loading, audio processing pipeline). Also read ../whisper-web/src/ directly for implementation details. Prefer WebGPU backend for faster inference (falls back to WASM if unavailable). Adapt to our React app structure — don't copy wholesale.
